text:
Maya R: Hey team — quick question. I had a telemed visit for my daughter while I was out on parental leave and the provider's claim isn't showing as in-network on the portal. Do I need to file anything manually?
Priya S: sorry to hear that, is the provider listed under the plan network lookup? can you DM the provider name and date? :eyes:
Maya R: I checked the provider lookup and they come up as 'Affiliated provider' but not explicitly in-network for our plan. visit was 2026-03-12 with "Northstar Pediatrics Telehealth".
Benefits Team: Thanks Maya — two quick paths: 1) if the provider is actually in-network but the lookup is lagging, we can help route a direct claim submission; 2) if they are out-of-network, you can submit for reimbursement (usually billed at allowed amount). Can you share the provider invoice/EOB?
Maya R: Uploading screenshot and invoice now. link: https://redwood-cloud/internal-uploads/claims/1823004321-maya-invoice.png
benefits-bot: Automated reply: Hi! For telemedicine while on approved leave, services are covered under Basic Care plan B if provider is in-network. If out-of-network, submit a "Member Reimbursement Claim" with itemized receipt and provider info. See https://docs.redwood.com/benefits/submit-claim (internal).
Jordan L: FYI if provider has NPIs that map to a larger group, sometimes the directory shows the group not the telehealth platform. We had a similar case last quarter.
Priya S: Maya — please send the following to benefits@redwood.com with subject "Reimbursement request — Maya R — 03/12/2026":
```
1) Member name, DOB, and employee ID
2) Date of service: 03/12/2026
3) Provider name: Northstar Pediatrics Telehealth
4) Itemized invoice / receipt (PDF)
5) Provider NPI or tax ID if available
6) Explanation of why provider listed as affiliated (optional)
```
Priya S: Expected timeline: we forward to carrier within 2 business days; carrier adjudication ~7–21 business days. If it's out-of-network, typical reimbursement checks/EFT arrive in 2–6 weeks.
Maya R: Thanks — one follow-up: I'm currently traveling (out of state) — does that affect anything?
Benefits Team: Travel doesn't affect reimbursement eligibility. One note: if provider billed as out-of-network and carrier denies, we can file an appeal. If this was an urgent/emergency consult while traveling internationally, there are special clauses — mention "urgent/remote care while traveling" in the email and attach boarding pass/itinerary if relevant.
Maya R: Got it. Sending email now.
Priya S: Once you send, ping us here and we'll track it through. :thumbsup:
Maya R: Sent — benefits@redwood.com. Subject line as requested. Attachment: invoice.pdf, telemed-session-log.txt
Benefits Team: Received — we got your case #BR-8269. We'll update you when carrier responds; feel free to @Priya S or @Jordan L if you don't hear in 10 business days.
Maya R: appreciate it, thanks everyone! :pray:
